title: The TRUTH About Organic Food and is it Worth it? Dr Yvonne Burkart
summary: Interview with a food-safety advocate: organic reliably lowers pesticide exposure but does not address heavy metals, partly because conventional compost is allowed.

assertions.quote: organic promise of less exposure to pesticides absolutely holds true
water and wind, inadvertent drift occurs and that's kinda how some pesticide contamination can occur
when it comes to heavy metals, it's outside the scope
the National Organic program allows the use of conventional compost

verdicts.note: NOP allows manure and compost from non-organic livestock, but evidence that this raises heavy metals in organic crops is limited.

7 CFR 205.203(c) allows raw and composted animal manure without requiring it to come from organic animals, but requires managing it so it does not contaminate crops, soil or water with heavy metals; the rule shows the allowance and recognizes the heavy-metal risk, not how often contamination happens.

assertions.quote: It also doesn't allow certain types of processes and GMOs
